title: Provider-supplied result URLs fetched with urlretrieve without scheme/host check (file:// local read, arbitrary-host fetch)
description: The KIE task-status response field resultJson.resultUrls[0] (and Suno audio_url / resultUrls in make_song.py) goes unchanged to urllib.request.urlretrieve with a destination filename. CPython's urlretrieve uses urlopen's default opener, which includes FileHandler, FTPHandler and DataHandler and allows any http(s) host. With a filename, a file: URL is copied byte for byte from local disk into the output directory (stdlib docstring: 'If a filename is passed and the URL points to a local resource, the result is a copy from local file to new file'). The premise is a malicious, compromised or spoofed response from api.kie.ai. The tools reach that host over HTTPS with a proxy-injected key, so this is a defense-in-depth gap at a third-party trust boundary, not an unauthenticated entry. Source shows the following onward effects in run_set.py. The copied file is decoded with cv2.VideoCapture (judge.frames). Its frames are put into grid.jpg, which is uploaded to KIE's upload host and sent to a vision model. The clip is also re-encoded into the assembled OUT/video.mp4. Only local files that OpenCV and ffmpeg can decode as video or image (for example other local media of the family) give visible frames. Other files (keys, configs) are copied into OUT but are not decoded or sent anywhere by this path. The frames go back to the same provider whose response started the chain. An http(s) URL to an internal host gives only a GET from the operator's machine whose body is saved locally.
claimed_root_cause: There is no allowlist on scheme (https) or host (the expected KIE result host) before the urllib.request.urlretrieve calls that consume provider-controlled URLs, and the default urllib opener honors file:, ftp: and data: schemes.

trace.description: K.req('GET', /api/v1/jobs/recordInfo) returns provider-controlled JSON from https://api.kie.ai into d
url = json.loads(d['resultJson'])['resultUrls'][0] with no scheme or host validation
urllib.request.urlretrieve(url, cp['file']) writes to OUT/<k>.mp4; a file: URL copies a local file there, and any http(s) host or ftp:/data: URL is also accepted
J.judge(c['file'], ...) is called on the downloaded or copied file
cv2.VideoCapture(clip) decodes the file; only decodable media gives frames
decoded frames are written into grid.jpg and passed to AP.vision
grid image is uploaded via kie_compare.upload to kieai.redpandaai.co and sent to the vision model (the clip is also concatenated into OUT/video.mp4 by the ffmpeg concat at tools/run_set.py:202)

evidence.description: urlretrieve on the unvalidated provider URL, with a destination filename
same pattern: urlretrieve(x['resultUrl'], file) from recordInfo resultJson
same pattern: urlretrieve(url, f) from recordInfo resultJson
same pattern: urlretrieve(url, songN.mp3), where url is a provider audio_url or resultUrls item
API host is https://api.kie.ai: the response that starts the chain comes from the credentialed provider over TLS, so exploitation needs a compromised or malicious provider
upload() reads local file bytes into a multipart body that is POSTed to the KIE upload host (line 46). This is the leg auto_plan.photo_url uses to send the judge grid out

blockers: The required OS-enforced sandbox is unavailable in this run, so no harness could show urlretrieve copying a file:// URL inside Run.poll, or show OpenCV decoding the copied file into grid frames

The premise is a malicious, compromised or spoofed recordInfo response from the credentialed HTTPS provider. Whether KIE can return attacker-influenced resultUrls is provider behavior that source cannot show

validation_plan.local: In an offline sandbox with an empty environment, monkeypatch kie_compare.req so recordInfo returns {'data':{'state':'success','creditsConsumed':0,'resultJson':'{"resultUrls":["file:///<scratch>/dummy.mp4"]}'}}. Stub kie_compare.upload and auto_plan.vision to record their arguments without network. Run Run.poll on one dummy clip with keys=[k]. Check that OUT/<k>.mp4 is a byte copy of <scratch>/dummy.mp4. Then call judge.judge on it and check that the stubbed upload receives a grid.jpg built from dummy.mp4's frames. Repeat with file:///<scratch>/dummy.txt (non-media) and check that it is copied but not decoded or uploaded. Regression: after adding a check that urlparse(url).scheme == 'https' and the host is on a pinned KIE result-host allowlist, both mocks must be refused before any file is written.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner reviews a few real recordInfo results already saved locally (state.json / task.json in past OUT folders) to list the result hosts KIE actually returns, so the allowlist can be pinned. The owner also confirms whether any request field the tools send (prompt, image_urls) can influence resultUrls. Send no audit traffic to KIE.

title: Shared-DB tap coordinates are printed unquoted into the run_set.py argument line the operator runs in a shell (command/argument injection)
description: db_photos.py rebuilds the uploaded photos from an exported copy of the test page's Artifact DB and prints the run_set.py photo arguments. It appends '@x,y' built verbatim from session/photos items[].subject (tools/db_photos.py:28-29) and prints the list space-joined with no quoting (line 32). The documented operator workflow (PROJECT_STATE.md:327 and :489-490) substitutes that printed line as <args> into `python3 tools/run_set.py OUT <args> --max-credits <balance-10>`, run in the operator's Bash session. The page itself only writes rounded numbers (tools/transition-test.html:219), and savePhotos (:177) stores whatever subject value the client holds. Nothing on the read side checks that x/y are numbers. A principal who can write the shared DB doc could set subject.x to a string containing shell metacharacters (';', '$(...)'), which run when the line is pasted literally. They could also set extra arguments such as '--max-credits 1e9' or an extra local image path, which survive word splitting. argparse in run_set.py (:209-212) accepts optionals mixed with the photos positional list, so the paid-credit cap could be lifted, or a local file could be sent to the provider. The float() parse of the tap (run_set.py:54, align_faces.py:53) runs only after the shell has already parsed the line. Exploitability depends on two facts outside the source: someone other than the owner must be able to write the artifact DB, and the operator (the owner or Claude) must transcribe the printed line literally into the shell.
claimed_root_cause: db_photos.py treats session/photos items[].subject.x/subject.y from a schema-less shared Artifact database as trusted numbers. It interpolates them into a shell-destined argument string with no numeric validation or shlex quoting (tools/db_photos.py:28-29, 32).

trace.description: session/photos is written to the shared Artifact DB with subject copied as-is and no schema. Any principal with write access to the artifact's DB can store arbitrary JSON (strings) in subject.x/y. The legitimate UI writes only numbers (line 219).
The exported session/photos.json is loaded with json.load and has no type checks.
s = it.get('subject') is taken directly from the DB item.
f"@{s['x']},{s['y']}" interpolates the raw values; spaces, ';', '$(' and '--option' strings are kept intact.
print(' '.join(args)) emits the unquoted argument line intended for the shell.
The printed line is used as <args> in `python3 tools/run_set.py OUT <args> --max-credits <balance-10>`, executed in the operator's Bash session (repeated at lines 489-490).

evidence.description: args.append(dst + (f"@{s['x']},{s['y']}" if s else "")): no float() conversion and no shlex.quote.
print(" ".join(args)): output is space-joined and unquoted.
The tap is parsed with float() only inside run_set, after the shell has already tokenized and interpreted the line.

--max-credits (default 1200) is the paid-credit cap an injected argument could override; --use-clips (line 211) can also be injected. argparse accepts these mixed in with the nargs='+' photos positional.
Workflow step: the db_photos.py output is used as `<photos with @x,y taps>` in the run_set.py command (line 490), run in the background.
The legitimate page writes subject as rounded numbers only, so the intended type is numeric; nothing on the read side enforces it.

blockers: Who can write the artifact's shared DB (session/photos) is decided by claude.ai sharing and is not visible in source. If only the owner can write it, this is self-injection and not a vulnerability.

Whether the operator (the owner or a Claude session) transcribes the printed line literally into a shell command, or reviews or reconstructs it, is an operational fact outside source. Literal transcription enables command execution; $(...) substitution enables argument injection only.
The OS-enforced execution sandbox is unavailable in this run, so db_photos.py was not executed against a malicious fixture. The printed-output behavior is established from source reading only.

validation_plan.local: In a sandbox with no network, an empty environment, a read-only repository and a scratch-only writable directory SCRATCH: create SCRATCH/DB/session/photos.json = {"items":[{"id":"a","subject":{"x":"0.5,0.5 --max-credits 1e9 ;touch SCRATCH/pwned;#","y":0}}]} and SCRATCH/DB/photodata/a-0.json = {"id":"a","k":0,"n":1,"b64":"AA=="}. Run `python3 tools/db_photos.py SCRATCH/DB SCRATCH/out > SCRATCH/line` with a 10 s wall-clock limit. Check that SCRATCH/line contains the unquoted ';', '#' and '--max-credits 1e9'. Then run `printf '%s\n' $(cat SCRATCH/line)` to show that word splitting yields a separate '--max-credits' token. Do not run run_set.py and do not evaluate the line in a shell.
validation_plan.deployment: The owner opens the sharing settings of the test page artifact and records whether anyone besides the owner has edit access that lets them write the page's shared database. Separately, the owner confirms whether the printed db_photos.py line is pasted verbatim into the run_set.py command. Recommended fix either way: in db_photos.py, convert subject.x/y with float() and require 0 <= value <= 1 (reject otherwise), and print each argument with shlex.quote. Alternatively, have run_set.py read the taps directly from the JSON instead of from a pasted command line.
